title: Word Search
summary: Decide whether a word can be traced through neighbouring cells of a letter grid without reusing a cell.

tests.explain: S (row 0) → T below it → A to the right → R → E above R. Every step moves to a neighbouring cell.
T → O → N → E works, but no S touches that E, so the word can't be finished.
The board has only one A, and a cell can't be used twice in the same word.

hints: Try every cell as the start of the word. From a cell that matches word[i], the next letter must be in one of its 4 neighbours.
Write dfs(r, c, i): fail if (r, c) is off the board or board[r][c] !== word[i]; succeed if i is the last index. Otherwise recurse into the 4 neighbours with i + 1.
To stop a path from reusing a cell, overwrite board[r][c] with a marker like "#" before recursing and put the letter back afterwards, whether the branch succeeded or not.

complexity.time: O(m · n · 3^L) for an m × n board and a word of length L: each start explores at most 3 new directions per letter (it can't step back onto the cell it came from)
complexity.space: O(L) for the recursion depth; cells are marked in place instead of in a visited set
